no single assay ties a measured release amount to a measured bacterial count at the same instant; the two time series run in parallel windows (8-168h release vs 24-168h survival) but are not a matched dose-response, so the association is suggestive of coincidence in timing, not a demonstrated causal or dose-dependent link between amount released and degree of killing.

the lower survival for Ampicillin scaffolds versus drug-free scaffolds could reflect ampicillin's antibacterial action occurring independently of the specific release kinetics or structural state emphasized in A (i.e., any comparable ampicillin exposure might have produced similar killing), so the pair does not establish that it is specifically the 2Co degradation-linked release profile, rather than ampicillin's presence generically, that drives the survival decline.
